summary: Kosen Imakita (1816–1892) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Togai Fujisawa, Kyokuso Hirose, Daisetsu Jōen at Shokoku-ji, and Gisan Zenrai at Sōgen-ji. He served as abbot of Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892).
Koshin Suzuki (born 1959) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a researcher (attested 1995–1998).

Koshiro Tamaki (1915–1999) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo, he held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1964–1976), Tohoku University (~1976–1979), and Nihon University (1979–1986).

Kosho Kawamura (born 1924) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura, later serving at Toyo University until 1994 and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 2001).

Kosho Uchiyama (1912–1998) was active in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied Western philosophy at Waseda University and trained under Kodo Sawaki (1941–1965). Uchiyama taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (~1937–1940) and served as abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).

Koshu Itahashi (1927–2020) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy (~1944–1945), Sendai Daiichi High School (~1945–1949), and Tohoku University (~1949–1953) under Teruji Ishizu.

Kotatsu Fujita (1928–2023) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Harvard University, he served as a professor at Hokkaido University (~1968–1986) and as former president of Sapporo Otani Junior College (1992).
Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1925 to 1928 and later held a post at Taisho University.

Koyo Sakaino (1871–1933) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He held academic posts at Toyo University (~1900–1923) and Komazawa University (~1905–1925), and founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi and held a post as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1995).

Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) specialized in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his BA, MA, and doctorate at the University of Tokyo, and served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (1972–2000), among other academic appointments.

Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Senmyō. He served as head priest of Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), and taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881).

Kozui Otani (1876–1948) worked in Buddhist, Central Asian, and historical studies. He studied at Gakushuin, Kyoritsu Gakusha, and under Eun Maeda. He served as the 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914) and was a fellow of the Royal Geographical Society (~1902).
Kripa Shankar Shukla (1918–2007) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology who held posts at the University of Lucknow, serving through 1959 and attested there in 1976.

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sanskrit College and University (~1853–1857) and Presidency University (~1857–1860). He held posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui (1898–1982) was an Indology scholar educated at Sanskrit College, Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jagannath Barooah College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College under Alexander Duff. He served at Hare School (~1828–1832) and as Second Professor at Bishop's College (1852).

Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi (1918–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Bangalore University, Upakulapati at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha (attested 1997), and Honorary Director of the Dvaita Vedanta Studies and Research Foundation (attested 1997).

Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indology scholar who studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient and as an editorial board member for Studies on the History of Śaivism (both attested 2021).
